content: The more you try to hold on to your life, the more elusive it becomes. It is like trying to clasp water in your hand.
author: Alan Watts
sourceWork: The Book: On the Taboo Against Knowing Who You Are (1966)
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Water is the softest thing on earth, yet it carves through solid granite. It doesn't fight obstacles; it yields, flows around them, and quietly finds its way to its natural level.

Alan Watts understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. When we force outcomes with brute willpower and anxiety, we exhaust ourselves and create unnecessary resistance. Aligning with nature means trusting the timing of things and moving with steady, patient persistence.
reflectionPrompt: How does adopting this philosophical view alter the way you handle current friction?
